changes: Internal shared source reads defer their release authorization to the transformed output release. Cold producers still authorize before reading upstream or legacy bytes. Raw callers still authorize on source release.
Binary fallback output now also checks lifecycle and authorization after copying.
Unacceptable encoding responses explicitly authorize before returning 406.
Webview removes its second pre-content authorization; initial page authorization and final output authorization remain.
Non-Markdown webview assets negotiate and serve cached gzip directly with Vary and Content-Length; Markdown wrapping and sandbox headers remain.

validation.raceIntegration: passed, 17.177s server; shared source/result/HTTP, fallback, legacy cache, metadata contracts
newCoverage: One authorization per warm transformed file
Revocation during cold fill rejects final transformed output
Gzip website response decodes to same anonymized content as file
Website GET/HEAD deny revoked access and preserve sandbox

limitations: Three serial samples on a small GitHub App fixture with existing source caches, not a load test. Website live fixture is a file asset, not a large Markdown page or directory listing. Gzip encoding and decoded parity additionally tested using a larger local fixture.
remainingWebsiteCost: Webview still scans repository metadata to resolve anonymized paths and directory indexes. A dedicated collision-aware index would improve large repositories; the existing file index has different collision behavior and cannot be substituted directly.
